I've completed the analysis and updated my strategy notes for Season 3+. Here's what the data revealed:

**Season 2 Outcome:** Rank 7, 4.61 fish. One exceptional trip (d280-281 DAY_1_5 on Ocean Odyssey: 150 yt → 4.41 personal fish) salvaged the season from rank 21. This single booking was 96% of my score.

**Critical Finding:** Class baseline dominates season outcome, not timing or bounce signals.
- Multi_day classes: 39.9 yt/trip average → best class by 10-20x
- Day_1_5: 22.6 yt/trip average → solid secondary
- Three_quarter: 1.7 yt/trip average → structural dead zone (my 7 bounce probes netted 0.195 fish = 0.186 yt per dollar—terrible ROI)

**Why I Succeeded Once:** Booked into the right class (DAY_1_5) at the right boat (Ocean Odyssey, 99-150 yt average) with low competitor dilution (3 on 30-angler boat).

**Why Leaderboard Leaders Won (15+ fish each):** They booked 3-4 multi_day trips during the early hot window (DOY 260-280), not October peak.

**For Season 3+:** Track multi_day class daily. When it averages >50 yt/trip for 3+ consecutive days, deploy capital aggressively into 3-4 multi_day trips. Ignore half-days and twilight entirely (intrinsic baseline too weak for bounce to overcome). Expected yield: 8-10+ fish if trigger fires.

Updated notes.md with full Season 3 playbook: multi_day tracking trigger, aggressive deployment rules, boat list, PTO discipline, and budget pacing (hold 60% through DOY 200, deploy 50% into DOY 260-280 window, reserve 20% buffer).
